# Migrating to Product Builder v2.4.0

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/migration_guide.py — do not edit. Edit changelog.md (its `### Upgrading` subsection) and run `python3 .github/scripts/migration_guide.py write`. -->

**Release** v2.4.0 · 2026-10-31 · **Registry schema** 13 · **Kind** minor over v2.3.0

This page gets a project from **any earlier release** to v2.4.0. Find your version in the table, follow the five steps, and read the notes for every release your row says you cross.

## 1 · Find the version you are on

- **Plugin:** the `pb vX.Y.Z` badge in the prototype's meta-nav, the `· pb vX.Y.Z` line in the `/pb:preview` banner, or the first line of `prototype.html` (`<!-- pb-shell vX.Y.Z · rendered … -->`).
- **Registry:** `meta.schemaVersion` in your `registry.json`. No field means schema 2.

*Registry schema* is what that release wrote. If you skipped `/pb:update-version` back then, your registry is older; the dry run in step 3 reads the real value and plans from it.

## 3 · Upgrade, in this order

1. **Update the plugin.** `/plugin marketplace update product-builder`, then **restart Claude Code** so the new commands load. If a same-name marketplace blocks it: uninstall the plugin → remove the marketplace → add the source again → install.
2. **Read the notes your row links to** (section 4) and do what they say — renamed commands, changed defaults, anything no tool does for you. Replace any command your row lists as gone (section 6).
3. **Bring the registry to schema 13.** `/pb:update-version` (a dry run: it prints the plan and writes nothing), then `/pb:update-version --apply`. It backs up `registry.json` first. Skip this when your row says *none*.
4. **Re-render.** `/pb:build --render`, or restart `/pb:preview`. Until you do, `prototype.html` keeps showing the old shell.
5. **Check it worked.** The badge reads `pb v2.4.0`; `/pb:test --drift` reports no shell drift; `/pb:test` runs clean.

**If something goes wrong:** `/pb:update-version --rollback` restores the registry from the backup step 3 took. It is a file restore, so use it before you build on top; after that, `/pb:update-version --to <N>` runs the real reverse migrations. Background on the three version layers: [upgrading.md](../upgrading.md).

## 4 · Notes for the releases you cross

<a id="notes-v240"></a>

### v2.4.0

#### Upgrading

No schema step and no registry change. These change as soon as the plugin updates:

- **Previewing from another device or through a tunnel needs a flag.** Start it with
  `serve.py registry.json --ensure --host 0.0.0.0 --allow-host <name>`. Without it, the Host guard answers 403.
- **Preview URLs change once.** A project without a `.claude/launch.json` port moves from 8000 to its own port.
- **A page that links to `memory/` or a dot-path as a static asset now gets 403.** Move the asset, for
  example under `public/`.
- **A hand-off can stop on scanner findings** that older versions never reported. Review them, or pass
  `--accept-findings`.
- **Project copies of agents in `.claude/agents/` keep their old settings.** Re-run `agents_install.py`, or
  delete them and use the plugin's `pb:pb-*` agents.
- **Rendered pages grow by about 193 KB** for the self-hosted font.

<a id="notes-v200"></a>

### v2.0.0

#### Removed — BREAKING

**Twenty-four commands became twelve, and the twelve retired names were deleted rather than
aliased.** This is the whole reason 2.0.0 is a major. An old name is not redirected — it reports
that no such command exists. Nothing in an existing project stores these names; they live in habits
and in team docs.

| Retired | Run instead |
|---|---|
| `/pb:flow` · `/pb:sync-flow` | `/pb:plan --flow` |
| `/pb:data` · `/pb:sync-erd` | `/pb:plan --data` |
| `/pb:check-drift` | `/pb:test --drift` |
| `/pb:validate` | `/pb:handoff --tier=host` |
| `/pb:preview-ds` | `/pb:preview`, then the `/design-system` route |
| `/pb:build-check-design-system` | `/pb:build` — now §3a of the loop, automatic |
| `/pb:build-figma-handoff` | `/pb:handoff` → mode 3 (Figma) |
| `/pb:handoff-close` · `/pb:hand-off` | `/pb:handoff` → mode 1 (everything) |
| `/pb:handoff-dev` | `/pb:handoff` → mode 2 (engineering) |

[AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) §2 requires a backward-compat alias for every rename, to be dropped only in
a later major. These shipped without one, so by §2's own logic the release carrying them is that
major (**D-34**). The aliases are not added retroactively — a major is precisely where a removal is
allowed to land, and stubbing twelve commands would buy a smaller version number in exchange for
twelve more files to keep in step.

**Upgrading an existing project takes about five minutes:
[docs/upgrade-to-2.0.md](../../docs/upgrade-to-2.0.md).**

Full walkthrough: [upgrade-to-2.0.md](../upgrade-to-2.0.md).

#### Removed

- `docs/v0.4.0/` (SpecKit-era SRS / architecture / orchestrator / execution-plan), `docs/CHANGES-from-v0.4.0.md` (superseded by this changelog), and `docs/code-to-figma-handoff-research-brief.md` (research now implemented as the `/pb:build-figma-handoff` G-FP gates) — all retained in git history.

## 5 · Registry schema steps

`/pb:update-version` runs, in order, every step after your registry's schema. Each is one migration in `pb/migrations/`.

| Step | Schema | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0001 | 2 → 3 | v1.4.0 | v1.2 → v1.3: add meta.device, components[].scope, structured flow/erd shape (legacy html preserved). |
| 0002 | 3 → 4 | v1.4.1 | v1.3 → v1.4: extract inline render bodies to render/{components,screens}/<id>.js files (renderSrc); registry becomes pure data. |
| 0003 | 4 → 5 | v1.6.0 | v1.4 → v1.6: add meta.platform (default "web") and meta.dsSource (null until a DS is cloned) — the DS-truth provenance fields. |
| 0004 | 5 → 6 | v1.7.0 | v1.6 → v1.7: add meta.outputTier (default "host") and meta.exportTarget (null until set) — the code-export tier fields. |
| 0005 | 6 → 7 | v1.8.0 | v1.7 → v1.8: add meta.entry ("prd" / "figma", default "prd") — the intake provenance. |
| 0006 | 7 → 8 | v1.11.0 | v1.8 → schema 8: `tokens` becomes a W3C DTCG document ({ value, kind } → { $value, $type }) — standards-compliant, Figma/Style-Dictionary round-trippable. |
| 0007 | 8 → 9 | v1.11.0 | schema 8 → 9: atomic `level` is now required on every component (atom/molecule/organism/template); screens are `page`. Component-first / atomic-design law. |
| 0008 | 9 → 10 | v1.11.0 | v1 schema 9 → 10: extract inline anatomy/spec/usage/uiLogic to spec/{components,screens}/<id>.json sidecars (specSrc); registry sheds its bulkiest fields. |
| 0009 | 10 → 11 | v2.0.0 | v1 schema 10 → 11: add the logic contract (logic/{components,screens}/<id>.json via logicSrc, prose COPIED into notes[] and left in place), the `ia` slice, and registry.runtime[]; nothing is deleted, so the rollback is lossless. |
| 0010 | 11 → 12 | v2.0.0 | v1 schema 11 → 12: meta.tradeoffs[] collapses into ia.rules[] — each trade-off becomes a rule of kind 'decision' carrying decision{question, options[], chose, why}, and a [SUPERSEDED …] title prefix becomes decision.status. The field is emptied, not removed (AGENTS.md §3); rollback refills it (list-authored `options` return as 'A / B'). |
| 0011 | 12 → 13 | v2.1.0 | v1 schema 12 → 13: component spec sidecars take the Specs-plugin shape — anatomy{part:{type}} + layout + elements{styles, visibleWhen} + shape, measured by spec_measure.py; legacy anatomy.parts[]/spec.stack[] kept under `legacy`, prose under anatomyNote/specNote. |

<details><summary>Hand-applied notes some steps print at <code>--apply</code> (for <code>memory/constitution.md</code>, never written for you)</summary>

- **0002** — Render bodies are now real files under render/components/ and render/screens/. Edit those .js files directly (lint/diff them like any code); the registry's renderSrc field points at each one. /pb:build --render still regenerates prototype.html. Do NOT re-add inline `render` strings.
- **0003** — The design system is now a cloned, verifiable source. Run /pb:pull-ds to clone your DS into design-system/<name>/ (+ registry tokens + a .source.json snapshot); meta.dsSource then records where it came from and meta.platform its platform. /pb:test --drift will audit the clone against that source. No constitution edit is required — these fields default safely (platform "web", dsSource null).
- **0004** — Projects can now export code via /pb:handoff --tier=host|scaffold|hardened. Record the intended export target in the Stack Lock of memory/constitution.md (e.g. "Export target: react-tailwind") — meta.exportTarget mirrors it for the tooling. No constitution edit is auto-applied; defaults are safe (tier "host", target null == the existing runnable-prototype behavior).
- **0005** — Projects can now be born from a Figma frame via /pb:init --figma (meta.entry = "figma") in addition to a PRD (meta.entry = "prd", the default). Unmapped Figma layers are logged to gaps.md as labeled placeholders — never invented components. No constitution edit is required; the default "prd" preserves existing behavior.
- **0006** — Design tokens are now authored in the W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) format: each token is `{ "$value": ..., "$type": ... }` (space/size/radius/fontSize all map to $type "dimension"). The document stays flat, so `var(--name)` in render bodies is unchanged. Update the constitution's token principle to name the DTCG standard; a cloned DS may add nested groups + `{alias}` references (also valid DTCG).
- **0007** — Component-first is now enforced: every component declares an atomic `level` and only `atom` render bodies may emit raw HTML primitives — molecules/organisms/screens must be pure composition via pbUse() of lower-level components (lint R-LEVEL / R-COMPOSE / R-LEVEL-ORDER, ERROR under --strict). Add the component-first + atomic-composition law to the constitution, and note the rule that a component's level follows its DS-component granularity (a dsMatch'd component is an atom even if visually composite).
- **0008** — Component/screen handoff docs (anatomy, spec, usage, uiLogic) now live in spec/components/<id>.json and spec/screens/<id>.json, pointed at by each entry's `specSrc`. Edit those sidecar files directly; the UI Design spec drawer still shows them (render.py re-inlines them). Do NOT re-add inline anatomy/spec fields to registry.json.
- **0009** — Logic now has a home of its own: logic/components/<id>.json and logic/screens/<id>.json, pointed at by each entry's `logicSrc`. Two halves — `seam`/`handlers`/`disclosure` are DERIVED (rewritten by `logic_extract.py --contracts`; never hand-edit them), while `writes[]` and `affordances[].why` are yours to write and no tool will touch them.
  The migration COPIED existing `logicNotes`/`uiLogic` prose into `notes[]` with a pointer back to the original, which is still exactly where it was. Most of it is dated rationale that belongs in memory/decisions.md — move it there as you touch each item, then delete the copy. Nothing is deleted for you.
  Two new slices: `ia` (jobs + layers — author it at /pb:init or /pb:plan) and `runtime[]` (the project's own modules, inlined before every render body — a real file per entry, instead of a component whose render body returns '').
- **0010** — A trade-off is a rule, and is now stored as one. `meta.tradeoffs[]` is emptied (the field stays, per AGENTS.md §3): every entry is now an `ia.rules[]` rule of kind 'decision', carrying `decision{ question, options[], chose, why }` — `options[]` holds what LOST, which is the one thing a rule could not say for itself.
  ANY rule may carry a decision block, whatever its kind, and the Logic tab draws it on the card. A rule of kind 'decision' is one you have decided but not yet expressed as a state machine, a matrix or a constraint — when you do, change the kind and keep the block.
  /pb:clarify no longer captures trade-offs as a separate task: it authors the rule and its decision together, and still appends one entry per decision to memory/decisions.md.
- **0011** — Component specs are now MEASURED, not typed. spec/components/<id>.json carries `anatomy` (part → type), `layout`, `elements` (padding / item spacing / radius / colours, each mapped to a token when the value matches one) and `shape`; a part is optional iff it has `visibleWhen`. /pb:build re-measures a component on its next build (§3a runs `tools/spec_measure.py --component <id> --write`), which replaces the best-effort conversion this update made. Mark parts in render bodies with `data-part="<name>"` (design-component-build §3). Old structured anatomy/spec stay under `legacy` in each sidecar.

</details>

## 7 · What changed in v2.4.0

*Additive, no schema change. A field audit of real projects found the code sound and its rules out of
reach: they lived in a file that doesn't ship, so sessions worked around them. This release ships the
rules, closes what the audit proved open, and fixes what real sessions kept tripping over.*

- **The preview refuses a foreign Host on every route.** GET routes checked nothing, so a page using DNS
  rebinding could read the project through the browser, `.git/config` and `registry.json` included. Any
  `Host` that isn't loopback, the bound `--host` or an `--allow-host NAME` now gets a 403 naming the flag.
  Dot-paths, `memory/` and the registry are never served as static files (decided on the resolved path,
  casefolded), and responses carry `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, `SAMEORIGIN` and `same-origin` headers.
- **The preview stays up.** The 30-minute idle exit kept taking previews away mid-task, and agents answered
  with `--idle-exit 0`, leaving servers that never stopped. The default is now 8 hours. `serve.py registry.json
  --ensure` is the one idempotent start, detached and safe to repeat. Each project gets its own stable
  port instead of competing for 8000. At most 6 managed previews run per user (`PB_PREVIEW_MAX`): starting
  another stops the longest-idle one with no tab open, never one with a tab.
- **The security scanner is rebuilt.** It now finds GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Google, Stripe, Figma and JWT
  credentials, credentials in URLs, Bearer headers, and regional phone and national-ID formats in a
  one-line-per-country table. It also reads `runtime/`, stylesheets, spec and logic sidecars and candidates,
  and `--dir` scans a folder. False alarms on design-tool keys, data URIs, SVG paths, coordinates and
  numeric ids are gone: on three real projects, errors went from 23, 50 and 65 to zero.
- **Nothing leaves without a scan.** `/pb:handoff` scans first in every mode, and an error stops it unless
  accepted with `--accept-findings`, which is recorded. `/pb:init --import` says a bundle is code and its
  text is data.
- **The rules ship.** `pb/docs/canon.md` holds the operating rules, and no shipped file cites a repo-only
  document any more. Three plugin hooks put them in front of the model in any pb project: a short digest at
  session start, and one line of advice before a hand-written Playwright script, `--idle-exit 0`, a detached
  or killed preview, a hand-written registry write, or a browser MCP call. They advise only: they never
  block and never decide a permission.
- **A check ladder replaces "screenshot everything".** UI checks were about 17% of spend and 28 hours of
  waiting a month on five real projects. `pb/docs/canon.md` § *Checking a change* picks the lowest of five
  levels by change type. A new or restructured screen still gets every width.
- **`shot.py` covers what scripts were written for.** `--step` interleaves click, fill, press, wait, eval and
  screenshot. `--no-png` answers with facts and no image, which saves context rather than time. A timeout is
  a clean exit 3.
- **`slice.py` reaches `ia` and single list entries**, such as `get ia rules.<id>` and `set flow stories.<id>`.
  `logic_extract.py`, `logic_check.py` and `migrate_runner.py` accept a folder, a registry path or `--registry`.
- **`test_run.py` reports a navigation race as `blocked`** instead of crashing the run.
- **Third-party loads are checked.** Inter is self-hosted (SIL OFL 1.1), which adds about 193 KB to each
  rendered page. Mermaid is pinned with SRI, and when it can't load the canvas says so. `tests/shell_lint.py`
  fails on any cross-origin asset without an integrity attribute.
- **`--exec` has no route to the host.** The old context handed bodies a host function, so
  `console.log.constructor('return process')()` reached node. Bodies now run with a null-prototype global
  and no code generation from strings.
- **`/pb:clean` sees more:** `.pb-patches/` (`--keep-patches N`), `memory/decisions.md`
  (`--rotate-decisions`), and `.claude/worktrees/` (reported, never deleted).
- **`R-RETIRED`** warns when `meta.others` or `meta.tradeoffs` holds data. It never fails a run.
- **Working agents are pinned to Sonnet.** Eight agents inherited the caller's model, usually the most
  expensive one. `pb-explorer` is unchanged, and a per-dispatch `model` still overrides.
- **CI gains a macOS + Python 3.9 job**, the setup people actually run. It isn't a required check yet.
- **`/pb:init` git defaults:** new projects ignore `prototype.html`, `design-system.html`, `.preview/` and
  `.pb-patches/`.
- **Pick mode** (merged after the v2.3.0 tag) reaches users with this version.
- **Every release ships a migration guide.** `docs/migrations/v<version>.md` is generated from the
  git tags, `changelog.md`, `pb/migrations/` and `pb/commands/`. It covers the upgrade from any
  earlier release: a row per starting version with the schema steps `/pb:update-version` will run,
  the commands that are gone and the notes to read first, then the five-step upgrade, every schema
  step, the retired commands with what to run instead, and the changelog. `bump_version.py auto`
  writes it. The pipeline's bump-version job fails while it is missing or stale, and asks for a
  hand-written `### Upgrading` changelog subsection when a release is a major, changes the schema
  or removes a command. The draft GitHub Release puts the guide in its notes and attaches it as
  `MIGRATION-vX.Y.Z.md`. The guide for v2.3.0 is included.

### Upgrading

No schema step and no registry change. These change as soon as the plugin updates:

- **Previewing from another device or through a tunnel needs a flag.** Start it with
  `serve.py registry.json --ensure --host 0.0.0.0 --allow-host <name>`. Without it, the Host guard answers 403.
- **Preview URLs change once.** A project without a `.claude/launch.json` port moves from 8000 to its own port.
- **A page that links to `memory/` or a dot-path as a static asset now gets 403.** Move the asset, for
  example under `public/`.
- **A hand-off can stop on scanner findings** that older versions never reported. Review them, or pass
  `--accept-findings`.
- **Project copies of agents in `.claude/agents/` keep their old settings.** Re-run `agents_install.py`, or
  delete them and use the plugin's `pb:pb-*` agents.
- **Rendered pages grow by about 193 KB** for the self-hosted font.
